s0001.literal: In the second year, spring, first month, on xinwei new moon day, there was a solar eclipse.
s0001.idiomatic: In the second year, on the xinwei new moon of the first month of spring, the sun was eclipsed.

s0002.literal: On guiyou day, the Shandong surveillance commissioner reported: "Zhang Hong, chief commissioner of Zhending Circuit, formerly in Jinan, took advantage of the disturbance to embezzle government goods.
s0002.idiomatic: On guiyou day the Shandong surveillance commissioner reported that Zhang Hong, chief commissioner of Zhending Circuit, had embezzled government property while stationed in Jinan during the upheaval.

s0003.literal: " An edict noted that Hong had once reported Li Tan's rebellion, pardoned him from the death penalty, removed him from office, and ordered confiscation of the stolen goods for repayment to the government.
s0003.idiomatic: An edict noted that Hong had once reported Li Tan's rebellion, spared him the death penalty, dismissed him from office, and ordered the stolen goods seized and returned to the treasury.

s0004.literal: Zhang Bangzhi, wanhu of Pizhou, and others sold horses in violation of regulations; all were executed.
s0004.idiomatic: Zhang Bangzhi, wanhu of Pizhou, and others traded horses in defiance of the ban; all were put to death.

s0005.literal: An edict ordered the relocation to Zhongdu of artisans of all categories from Zhenhai, Baibalixian, and Qianqianzhou, providing fifteen thousand taels of silver as travel expenses.
s0005.idiomatic: An edict moved artisans of every trade from Zhenhai, Baibalixian, and Qianqianzhou to Zhongdu and granted them fifteen thousand taels of silver for travel.

s0006.literal: Eight hundred catapult artificers and craftsmen from Nu Huai and Temudai'er were also relocated to Zhongdu to build ships and transport grain.
s0006.idiomatic: Eight hundred catapult crews and craftsmen under Nu Huai and Temudai'er were also sent to Zhongdu to build ships and haul grain.

s0007.literal: On jimao day, the Beijing Circuit Branch Secretariat supplied ten thousand shi of travel grain to Jalichi households relocating eastward.
s0007.idiomatic: On jimao day the Beijing branch secretariat issued ten thousand shi of travel grain to Jalichi households moving east.

s0008.literal: Ne Huai, battle overseer of Dengzhou, and Dong Wenbing, wanhu of new and old armies, were both appointed deputy commanders-in-chief of Henan.
s0008.idiomatic: Ne Huai, battle overseer at Dengzhou, and Dong Wenbing, wanhu of the new and old armies, were both made deputy commanders-in-chief of Henan.

s0009.literal: On jiashen day, an edict strictly reinforced the prohibition on cross-border horse trading; violators were to be executed.
s0009.idiomatic: On jiashen day the Emperor strictly reinforced the ban on cross-border horse trading; violators would be executed.

s0010.literal: On yiyou day, wasteland in northern Henan was distributed among Mongol troops for cultivation.
s0010.idiomatic: On yiyou day wasteland in northern Henan was allotted to Mongol soldiers for farming.

s0011.literal: On wuzi day, Kokuochu, envoy of Prince Tachar, reached Huadao Post on the Beijing route and personally killed post clerks Hao Yong and Guo Heshang. An imperial order levied ten ingots of paper money from his master to redeem him from death.
s0011.idiomatic: On wuzi day Kokuochu, envoy of Prince Tachar, reached Huadao Post on the Beijing route and killed the clerks Hao Yong and Guo Heshang with his own hand. The Emperor ordered his master to pay ten ingots of paper money to redeem him from death.

s0012.literal: On gengyin day, the western city wall was extended to Xiada Road.
s0012.idiomatic: On gengyin day the western city wall was extended as far as Xiada Road.

s0013.literal: On guisi day, Buya of the Badongqir tribe came to court, presenting two thousand silver-fox pelts. He was granted nine of each of gold and plain silks, and eighteen bolts of brocade.
s0013.idiomatic: On guisi day Buya of the Badongqir tribe came to court with two thousand silver-fox pelts. He received nine pieces each of gold and plain silk and eighteen bolts of brocade.

s0014.literal: In Wucheng County, Lady Cui, wife of the Wang family, gave birth to three sons in one delivery.
s0014.idiomatic: In Wucheng County Lady Cui of the Wang clan gave birth to triplets.

s0015.literal: On dingyou day, two thousand shi of grain were allotted to the people under Prince Yulongdash.
s0015.idiomatic: On dingyou day two thousand shi of grain were granted to the people under Prince Yulongdash.

s0016.literal: King Wang Chon of Goryeo sent his younger brother, Prince Guangping Shun, bearing a memorial as tribute.
s0016.idiomatic: King Wang Chon of Goryeo sent his younger brother Prince Guangping Shun with a memorial and tribute.

s0017.literal: Second month, xinchou new moon: Commander Andong fought Song troops at Diaoyu Mountain, defeated them, and captured one hundred forty-six warships.
s0017.idiomatic: On the xinchou new moon of the second month Commander Andong fought the Song at Diaoyu Mountain, routed them, and took one hundred forty-six warships.

s0018.literal: On jiachen day, the Inner Palace Bureau was first established.
s0018.idiomatic: On jiachen day the Inner Palace Bureau was established for the first time.

s0019.literal: On wushen day, Prince Uludai was granted the seal of Prince of Hejian and given one thousand shi of rice for his people.
s0019.idiomatic: On wushen day Prince Uludai received the seal of Prince of Hejian and one thousand shi of rice for his followers.

s0020.literal: On dingsi day, the imperial carriage visited Shangdu.
s0020.idiomatic: On dingsi day the Emperor traveled to Shangdu.

s0021.literal: On guihai day, the six ministries were consolidated into four. Maimutding was made Minister of the combined Personnel and Rites Ministry, Ma Heng Minister of Revenue, Yan Zhongfan Minister of War and Justice, and Bieluding Minister of Works.
s0021.idiomatic: On guihai day the six ministries were merged into four: Maimutding became minister of personnel and rites, Ma Heng of revenue, Yan Zhongfan of war and justice, and Bieluding of works.

s0022.literal: Private brewing of saltpeter was forbidden in Shandong East Route.
s0022.idiomatic: Private distillation of saltpeter was banned in Shandong East Route.

s0023.literal: On jiazi day, Mongols were appointed darughachi for all circuits, Han Chinese as chief commissioners, and Muslims as deputy commissioners — this was made permanent policy.
s0023.idiomatic: On jiazi day Mongols were made darughachi in every circuit, Han Chinese chief commissioners, and Muslims deputy commissioners — a permanent arrangement.

s0024.literal: Baoheding, deputy commissioner of the Dongping Circuit Pacification Commission, was made Grand Councillor; Wang Jin, Shandong surveillance commissioner, was made Associate Councillor.
s0024.idiomatic: Baoheding, deputy commissioner of the Dongping pacification commission, was appointed grand councillor, and Wang Jin, Shandong surveillance commissioner, associate councillor.

s0025.literal: Lian Xixian and Shang Ting were dismissed.
s0025.idiomatic: Lian Xixian and Shang Ting were removed from office.

s0026.literal: An edict merged the civilian administration officers established by Prince Jibtemur.
s0026.idiomatic: An edict consolidated the civilian officials Prince Jibtemur had set up.

s0027.literal: An edict addressed the Patriarchate: "Monks who have mastered the Five Great Canon divisions shall be selected as finalists; those of moral standing shall be appointed state and prefectural Buddhist recorders, judges, chief and deputy abbots, and other posts. Three Doctrine Lecture halls and Three Chan assemblies shall still be established in each route."
s0027.idiomatic: An edict to the Buddhist patriarchate declared that monks who had mastered the Five Great Canon divisions would be chosen as finalists, and men of virtue would be appointed state and prefectural recorders, judges, chief and deputy abbots, and the like. Each route was still to maintain Three Doctrine Lecture halls and Three Chan assemblies.

s0028.literal: Third month, guiyou day: Guriyeo people raided and killed Kirimi troops. An edict ordered official grain, bows, and armor supplied to them.
s0028.idiomatic: In the third month, on guiyou day, Guriyeo raiders killed Kirimi soldiers. An edict ordered government grain, bows, and armor issued to the victims.

s0029.literal: On dinghai day, an edict ordered frontier troops to train in naval warfare and garrison farming.
s0029.idiomatic: On dinghai day an edict told frontier troops to drill in naval combat and garrison farming.

s0030.literal: The Song spy Li Fuzhu was executed.
s0030.idiomatic: Li Fuzhu, a Song spy, was put to death.

s0031.literal: On yiwei day, the north-south mutual market was abolished, southern goods among the populace were requisitioned, and the government paid their value.
s0031.idiomatic: On yiwei day the north-south border market was closed, southern goods held by private households were seized, and the government paid fair value.

s0032.literal: Eastern Liaoning suffered famine; ten thousand shi of grain and one hundred ingots of paper money were issued for relief.
s0032.idiomatic: Eastern Liaoning was starving; the court issued ten thousand shi of grain and one hundred ingots of paper money for relief.

s0033.literal: Summer, fourth month, wuwu day: Princes Hebichi and Eqilejin were each granted four plain silks and one gold piece for bowing.
s0033.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on wuwu day, Princes Hebichi and Eqilejin each received four bolts of plain silk and one gold piece for the bowing ceremony.

s0034.literal: Fifth month, renwu day: Four hundred fifty taels of silver were awarded for the campaign against Tibet by the troops under Wanhu Hulida'er.
s0034.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on renwu day, four hundred fifty taels of silver were granted for the Tibetan campaign fought by Wanhu Hulida'er's troops.

s0035.literal: On wuzi day, hunting by local people was forbidden in Beijing, Pingluan, and other places.
s0035.idiomatic: On wuzi day hunting by local residents was banned in Beijing, Pingluan, and neighboring districts.

s0036.literal: On gengyin day, an order stated: "When soldiers violate the law in camp, they must not be executed on authority; lesser offenses are to be punished and sent away, graver ones reported to the throne.
s0036.idiomatic: On gengyin day an order declared that soldiers who broke the law in camp could not be put to death on local authority: lighter crimes were to be punished and dismissed, heavier ones reported to the throne.

s0037.literal: " An edict exempted Shangdu from commercial taxes, liquor taxes, and other levies; the salt monopoly remained unchanged;
s0037.idiomatic: An edict exempted Shangdu from commercial taxes, liquor taxes, and similar dues, while the salt monopoly stayed as before;

s0038.literal: those who voluntarily moved to permanent homes had their households restored.
s0038.idiomatic: and anyone who voluntarily settled on permanent land had household obligations waived.

s0039.literal: An edict ordered garrison frontier troops in West Sichuan, Shandong, Nanjing, and other circuits to garrison-farm.
s0039.idiomatic: An edict ordered frontier garrisons in West Sichuan, Shandong, Nanjing, and other circuits to take up garrison farming.

s0040.literal: Intercalary fifth month, guimao day: Gaoxian was promoted to Jing Prefecture.
s0040.idiomatic: In the intercalary fifth month, on guimao day, Gaoxian was elevated to Jing Prefecture.

s0041.literal: On xinhai day, thirty thousand seven hundred twenty-four impoverished people without livestock among the followers of Prince Uludai were inspected; each person was given two dou five sheng of rice per month for four months.
s0041.idiomatic: On xinhai day a review found thirty thousand seven hundred twenty-four poor followers of Prince Uludai without livestock; each received two dou five sheng of rice monthly for four months.

s0042.literal: On bingchen day, the Diaomen Pacification Commissioner of Yazhou requested restoration of Diaomen city and towns; an edict ordered a survey.
s0042.idiomatic: On bingchen day the Diaomen pacification commissioner of Yazhou asked to rebuild Diaomen city and its towns; the Emperor ordered a survey.

s0043.literal: On guihai day, the Qin-Shu Branch Secretariat was moved to Xingyuan.
s0043.idiomatic: On guihai day the Qin-Shu branch secretariat was relocated to Xingyuan.

s0044.literal: On bingyin day, the Sichuan Branch Secretariat was ordered to divide troops for garrison farming.
s0044.idiomatic: On bingyin day the Sichuan branch secretariat was told to detach troops for garrison farming.

s0045.literal: On dingmao day, the subordinate prefectures of the four princes in Nanjing were divided: Zheng Prefecture was placed under Hethan, Jun Prefecture under Mingli, Sui Prefecture under Boluochi, and Cai Prefecture under Haidu; other subordinate counties were returned to the court.
s0045.idiomatic: On dingmao day the Nanjing prefectures held by four princes were reassigned: Zheng went to Hethan, Jun to Mingli, Sui to Boluochi, and Cai to Haidu; the remaining counties reverted to direct court control.

s0046.literal: Grand Councillor Zhao Bi was sent to administer branch secretariat affairs in Nanjing, Henan Prefecture, Daming, Shunde, Luoci, Zhangde, Huaimeng, and other circuits; Grand Councillor Lian Xixian to administer branch affairs in Dongping, Jinan, Yidu, Zilai, and other circuits; and Left Associate of the Central Secretariat Yao Shu to administer branch affairs in Xijing, Pingyang, Taiyuan, and other circuits.
s0046.idiomatic: Grand Councillor Zhao Bi was sent to run branch affairs in Nanjing, Henan Prefecture, Daming, Shunde, Luoci, Zhangde, Huaimeng, and neighboring circuits; Grand Councillor Lian Xixian in Dongping, Jinan, Yidu, Zilai, and the like; and Left Associate Yao Shu in Xijing, Pingyang, Taiyuan, and neighboring circuits.

s0047.literal: An edict stated: "In the prefectures and districts of all circuits, if they are ancient famous commanderies, have numerous households, and stand at vital points, they need not be merged or abolished.
s0047.idiomatic: An edict declared that prefectures and districts on every circuit that were ancient famous commanderies, densely populated, and strategically placed should not be merged or abolished.

s0048.literal: Those with fewer than one thousand households may be merged where merger is possible; each appanage shall be merged into the prefectural city to which it belongs.
s0048.idiomatic: Districts with fewer than one thousand households might be merged where feasible; each appanage was to be folded into its governing prefectural city.

s0049.literal: Scattered prefectures, districts, and commanderies with few households need not maintain separate record offices or gatekeeper offices; the prefectural and district officials shall concurrently administer the attached counties.
s0049.idiomatic: Scattered prefectures and districts with small populations need not keep separate record offices or gatekeeper offices; prefectural officials would directly oversee the attached counties.

s0050.literal: Households not yet registered on all circuits who hold corvée posts are to be reported."
s0050.idiomatic: Unregistered households on every circuit who held corvée posts were to be reported to the throne."

s0051.literal: Sixth month, wuchen new moon: Xinde Prefecture Pacification Commissioner Xiang Liang said: "When the whole city submitted inward, many soldiers and civilians who had scattered into the southern territories wished to return and submit; all beg to be summoned back.
s0051.idiomatic: On the wuchen new moon of the sixth month Xiang Liang, pacification commissioner of Xinde Prefecture, reported that when the city had surrendered intact many soldiers and civilians who had fled south wished to return and submit, and asked that they be summoned back.

s0053.literal: Liang was also ordered to move the newly surrendered soldiers and civilians he commanded to garrison Tongjiang County and administer Xinde Prefecture affairs.
s0053.idiomatic: Liang was also ordered to move his newly surrendered soldiers and civilians to garrison Tongjiang County and administer Xinde Prefecture.

s0054.literal: On xinwei day, Aju's troops were granted one thousand twenty-three plus ingots of paper money for horse prices.
s0054.idiomatic: On xinwei day Aju's command received slightly more than one thousand twenty-three ingots of paper money to cover horse prices.

s0055.literal: On bingzi day, the moon encroached upon the great star of the Heart constellation.
s0055.idiomatic: On bingzi day the moon passed the great star of the Heart constellation.

s0056.literal: On wuyin day, the Shandong Commandery was moved to Yizhou.
s0056.idiomatic: On wuyin day the Shandong command headquarters was transferred to Yizhou.

s0057.idiomatic: Wanhu Chongxi established a garrison at Shizilu.

s0058.literal: Zhengyang was restored; Tula was ordered to garrison it.
s0058.idiomatic: Zhengyang was restored, and Tula was ordered to hold it.

s0059.literal: On jimao day, Qi Prefecture was placed under Huaimeng Circuit.
s0059.idiomatic: On jimao day Qi Prefecture was placed under Huaimeng Circuit.

s0060.literal: King Wang Chon of Goryeo sent his minister Rong Yinbo bearing a memorial to congratulate the Emperor on his birthday.
s0060.idiomatic: King Wang Chon of Goryeo sent his minister Rong Yinbo with a memorial congratulating the Emperor on his birthday.

s0061.literal: The people under Qianhu Kokuochu lacked food; paper money was granted for relief.
s0061.idiomatic: The followers of Qianhu Kokuochu were short of food; the court granted paper money for relief.

s0062.idiomatic: Wang Jin was removed from office.

s0063.literal: Privy Council officials said: "Han soldiers who fled while on campaign from all circuits, impoverished households not yet registered, and those hidden by appanage holders on pretext of exemption should all be conscripted and sent to serve.
s0063.idiomatic: Privy council officials reported that Han soldiers who had deserted on campaign from every circuit, poor households not yet registered, and men hidden by appanage holders under false exemptions should all be drafted and sent to serve.

s0065.literal: An edict ordered branch secretariat officials and all army commanders, officers, and rank-and-file to serve in person; violators were to be punished.
s0065.idiomatic: An edict required branch secretariat officials and every army commander, officer, and soldier to serve in person; violators would be punished.

s0066.literal: Autumn, seventh month, xinyou day: Yidu suffered great locust plague and famine; an order was issued to sell government grain at reduced price for relief.
s0066.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on xinyou day, Yidu was ravaged by locusts and famine; the court ordered government grain sold at reduced price for relief.

s0067.literal: On guihai day, King Chen Guangbing of Annam sent envoys bearing a memorial as tribute.
s0067.idiomatic: On guihai day King Chen Guangbing of Annam sent envoys with tribute and a memorial.

s0068.literal: On jiazi day, an edict granted Guangbing the calendar for the third year of Zhiyuan.
s0068.idiomatic: On jiazi day the Emperor granted Guangbing the calendar for the third year of Zhiyuan.

s0069.literal: Eighth month, bingzi day: Zouping County of Jinan Circuit presented one stalk of auspicious fungus.
s0069.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on bingzi day, Zouping County in Jinan Circuit presented a stalk of auspicious fungus.

s0070.literal: On wuyin day, King Wang Chon of Goryeo sent envoys bearing local products as tribute.
s0070.idiomatic: On wuyin day King Wang Chon of Goryeo sent envoys with local products as tribute.

s0071.literal: On jimao day, all chief ministers were dismissed; Antong was made Right Chancellor of the Central Secretariat and Bayan Left Chancellor.
s0071.idiomatic: On jimao day every chief minister was dismissed. Antong became right chancellor of the Central Secretariat and Bayan left chancellor.

s0072.literal: On wuzi day, Xu Heng was summoned from Huaimeng and Yang Cheng from Yidu.
s0072.idiomatic: On wuzi day Xu Heng was summoned from Huaimeng and Yang Cheng from Yidu.

s0073.literal: The imperial carriage returned from Shangdu.

s0074.literal: Ninth month, wuxu day: Because there would soon be rites at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, great music masters were taken from Dongping to rehearse the ceremonial forms in advance.
s0074.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on wuxu day, with rites at the Imperial Ancestral Temple approaching, great music masters were brought from Dongping to rehearse the ceremony in advance.

s0075.literal: An edict ordered palisades planted along the Jiang-Huai frontier; Xu, Su, and Pi Prefectures were to supply corvée labor.
s0075.idiomatic: An edict ordered palisades erected along the Jiang-Huai frontier, with Xu, Su, and Pi Prefectures supplying corvée labor.

s0076.literal: On gengzi day, the imperial grandson Temür was born.
s0076.idiomatic: On gengzi day the imperial grandson Temür was born.

s0077.literal: On dingsi day, two hundred fifty taels of silver were awarded for the Hexi campaign fought under Prince Jibtemur.
s0077.idiomatic: On dingsi day two hundred fifty taels of silver were granted for the Hexi campaign fought under Prince Jibtemur.

s0078.literal: Winter, tenth month, jimao day: Sacrifice was offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
s0078.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on jimao day, sacrifice was offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

s0079.literal: On guiwei day, an edict ordered the households of Zhang Rou of Shuntian, Yan Zhongji of Dongping, Ma, chief commissioner of Hejian, Zhang Lin of Jinan, Shi Mo, chief commissioner of Taiyuan, and others changed to civilian registration.
s0079.idiomatic: On guiwei day an edict transferred the households of Zhang Rou of Shuntian, Yan Zhongji of Dongping, Chief Commissioner Ma of Hejian, Zhang Lin of Jinan, Chief Commissioner Shi Mo of Taiyuan, and others to civilian rolls.

s0080.literal: Ninety-three Song captives taken by soldiers under Commander Chaobuhua and Wanhu Huaidu were redeemed by the government and made civilians.
s0080.idiomatic: Ninety-three Song captives taken by soldiers under Commander Chaobuhua and Wanhu Huaidu were redeemed by the government and registered as civilians.

s0081.literal: Forty-five who had privately crossed the forbidden border and seized captives were permitted to reunite with relatives and farm in the interior.
s0081.idiomatic: Forty-five men who had privately crossed the forbidden border to seize captives were allowed to rejoin their families and farm in the interior.

s0082.literal: On wuzi day, an edict stated that private merchants on each route who had once entered the southern territories, if they reported themselves first, would be pardoned and enrolled as soldiers.
s0082.idiomatic: On wuzi day an edict promised that private merchants on every route who had once entered Song territory would, if they came forward first, be pardoned and drafted as soldiers.

s0083.literal: Eleventh month, bingshen day: Li Chang was summoned from Dongping.
s0083.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on bingshen day, Li Chang was summoned from Dongping.

s0084.literal: On xinchou day, Prince Jibtemur was granted twenty-five thousand taels of silver and one thousand ingots of paper money.
s0084.idiomatic: On xinchou day Prince Jibtemur received twenty-five thousand taels of silver and one thousand ingots of paper money.

s0085.literal: On guichou day, Yang Wen'an was awarded fifty taels of gold for battle merit; his troops received six hundred taels of silver and graded silks and brocades.
s0085.idiomatic: On guichou day Yang Wen'an received fifty taels of gold for battle merit, and his troops six hundred taels of silver plus graded silks and brocades.

s0086.literal: On jiazi day, an edict stated that soldiers incapacitated by age or hardship and unable to serve might combine two or three households into one regular soldier; where a household had only one able-bodied man, he might hire a substitute to serve.
s0086.idiomatic: On jiazi day an edict allowed soldiers broken by age or hardship and unfit for service to combine two or three households into one regular soldier, and where only one able-bodied man remained in a household, he might hire a substitute.

s0087.literal: Twelfth month, jisi day: More than two hundred twenty prefectures and counties were consolidated or abolished.
s0087.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jisi day, more than two hundred twenty prefectures and counties were merged or abolished.

s0088.literal: On gengwu day, Song Zizhen said: "Court and secretariat policy should not be issued and changed repeatedly.
s0088.idiomatic: On gengwu day Song Zizhen argued that court and secretariat policy should not be issued and changed so often.

s0089.literal: Moreover, the Ministry of Justice handles matters touching human life; Minister Yan Zhongfan is young — an elder versed in penal law should be chosen for the post.
s0089.idiomatic: The Ministry of Justice, he added, handled matters of life and death, yet Minister Yan Zhongfan was young; an elder versed in penal law should be appointed instead.

s0090.literal: " He also requested abolition of the Beijing Branch Secretariat and establishment of a separate Pacification Commission to control the northeastern prefectures and districts.
s0090.idiomatic: He also asked that the Beijing branch secretariat be abolished and a separate pacification commission set up to oversee the northeastern prefectures and districts.

s0092.literal: Informers at court and in the secretariat were forbidden so as to reduce litigation.
s0092.idiomatic: Informers at court and in the secretariat were banned to reduce litigation.

s0093.literal: On xinwei day, because the western frontier garrison under Prince Yesubhua had repeatedly won battle merit, three hundred taels of silver were awarded.
s0093.idiomatic: On xinwei day three hundred taels of silver were granted because the western frontier garrison under Prince Yesubhua had repeatedly won battle merit.

s0094.literal: On guiyou day, Zhang Dehui was summoned from Zhending and Tushan Gonglu from Weizhou.
s0094.idiomatic: On guiyou day Zhang Dehui was summoned from Zhending and Tushan Gonglu from Weizhou.

s0095.literal: On dingchou day, an edict addressed Goryeo and granted the calendar for the third year of Zhiyuan.
s0095.idiomatic: On dingchou day an edict addressed Goryeo and granted the calendar for the third year of Zhiyuan.

s0096.literal: On guiwei day, Liu Bingzhong was granted fifty taels of gold.
s0096.idiomatic: On guiwei day Liu Bingzhong received fifty taels of gold.

s0097.literal: On jiashen day, Bayan, Song Zizhen, and Yang Cheng were granted one thousand taels of silver and sixty ingots of paper money each.
s0097.idiomatic: On jiashen day Bayan, Song Zizhen, and Yang Cheng each received one thousand taels of silver and sixty ingots of paper money.

s0098.literal: On dinghai day, an edict ordered selection of ten thousand strong and brave men from the various wings to serve as palace guard soldiers.
s0098.idiomatic: On dinghai day an edict ordered ten thousand strong and brave men chosen from the various wings to serve as palace guard soldiers.

s0099.literal: On jichou day, the Great Jade Sea of Dushan was completed; an edict ordered the Hall of Broad Cold erected.
s0099.idiomatic: On jichou day the Great Jade Sea of Dushan was finished, and the Emperor ordered the Hall of Broad Cold built.

s0100.literal: That year, households numbered one million five hundred ninety-seven thousand six hundred one; silk ninety-eight thousand six hundred eighty-eight jin; and wrapped-silver paper money fifty-seven thousand six hundred eighty-two ingots.
s0100.idiomatic: That year registered households totaled one million five hundred ninety-seven thousand six hundred one; silk tribute ninety-eight thousand six hundred eighty-eight jin; and wrapped-silver paper money fifty-seven thousand six hundred eighty-two ingots.
